open3dApp.Visualization module

This module contains open3d window with the current scanned session. It also provides methods of communication and callbacks.

class open3dApp.Visualization.VisualizationApp(queue: Queue, o3d_to_f: Queue)[source]

Bases: object

Visualizes point clouds and other geometries.

Provides a running open3d application, which communicates with other processes via a Queue. Should be run on a different thread. Accepts LidarScan & OdometryData objects from the queue and displays them in the scene.

Important arguments:
_id – ID of a geometry in the scene.

Each geometry has a name (point clouds names start with ‘pcd_’) which ends with a unique ID. Adding a new geometry increments this index,

_queue – Queue from the Multiprocessing module.

It is used to accept data from other processes.

BARYCENTRE = 2
DOWNSAMPLE = 1
MENU_COORD_FRAME = 4
MENU_HEIGHT_MAP = 6
MENU_QUIT = 7

_add_pcd(pcd: open3d.geometry.PointCloud, name: str, color: List[float] = None)[source]
Adds / appends a new pcd to the scene.

If name does not exist in the #_scene_pcds dict then a new entry will be created. Otherwise, the new pcd will be appended to the specified point cloud and displayed in the scene.

Keyword Arguments:

  • frame. (pcd -- Correctly processed pcd, oriented in the right coordinate)

  • appended. (name -- Specifies to which pcd in the #_scene_pcds will the new pcd be)

  • colours. (color -- List of)

_monitor_server() → bool[source]
Monitors the state of the queue.

If new data is received, process it. If its is an instance of LidarData or OdometryData, accept it and display on the scene. Other data is discarded.

Returns:

True – when data from the queue has been accepted.

Scene is then redrawn with new content.

False – otherwise.

_o3d_to_f

Creates the window and adds the scene widget (basically are where we can draw stuff) Widget stores the real 3D scene, Window title based on the Operating system,
